scenes.line1: Why do some settings overwrite others?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why your Windows settings change unexpectedly? Let's see how Group Policy decides what sticks.
Group Policy applies in this order: local, site, domain, then organizational unit. The last one wins, so OU settings can override everything else.

scenes.title: Check which policies applied
scenes.say: If a setting isn't applying, use these commands to see which policies are active and force updates. This is a classic interview scenario.
An organizational unit organizes objects and links policies. Security groups grant permissions and filter users, but you can't link policies directly to them.

scenes.question: Can you link a GPO to a group?
scenes.right: No, GPOs link to organizational units. Groups are just for filtering.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: GPOs only link to organizational units, not groups. Groups are just for filtering.
